VIII.}}}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=8|verse=1|align=float}}{{dropinitial|A}}{{sc|Nd}} vve doe you to vnder{{ls}}tand, brethren, the grace of God, that is giuen in the churches of Macedonia, {{verse|chapter=8|verse=2|align=float}}† that in much experience of tribulation they had aboundance of ioy, & their very deepe pouertie abounded vnto the riches of their {{ls}}implicitie, {{verse|chapter=8|verse=3|align=float}}† for according to their povver (I giue them te{{ls}}timonie) and aboue their povver they vvere willing, {{verse|chapter=8|verse=4|align=float}}† vvith much exhortation reque{{ls}}ting vs the grace and communication of the mini{{ls}}terie that is done tovvard the {{ls}}aincts. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=5|align=float}}† And not as vve hoped, but their ovvne {{ls}}elues they gaue, fir{{ls}}t to our Lord, ∷ {{outside L|∷ The principal re{{ls}}pecte next after God, is to be had of our mai{{ls}}ters in religion, in al temporal and {{ls}}piritual dueties.}} then to vs by the vvil of God: {{verse|chapter=8|verse=6|align=float}}† in {{ls}}o much that vve de{{ls}}ired Titus, that as he began, {{ls}}o al{{ls}}o he vvould perfit in you this grace al{{ls}}o. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=7|align=float}}† But as in al things you abound in faith, and vvord, and knovvledge, & al carefulnes, moreouer al{{ls}}o in your charitie tovvard vs, that in this grace al{{ls}}o you may abounde. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=8|align=float}}† I {{ls}}peake not as commaunding: but by the carefulnes of others, approuing al{{ls}}o the good di{{ls}}po{{ls}}ition of your charitie. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=9|align=float}}† {{outside L|The Epi{{ls}}tle for S. Paulinus, ''Iun. 22.''}}For you knovv the grace of our Lord {{sc|Iesvs}} Chri{{ls}}t, that for you he vvas made poore, whereas he vvas riche: that by his pouertie you might be riche. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=10|align=float}}† And in this point I giue coun{{ls}}el: for this is profitable for you, vvhich haue begōne not only to doe, but al{{ls}}o to be willing, from the yere pa{{ls}}t: {{verse|chapter=8|verse=11|align=float}}† but novv perfourme ye it al{{ls}}o in deede: that as your minde is prompt to be vvilling, {{ls}}o it may be al{{ls}}o to perfourme, of that vvhich you haue. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=12|align=float}}† For if the vvil be prompt: it is accepted according to that vvhich it hath, not according to that vvhich it hath not. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=13|align=float}}† For not that other {{ls}}hould haue ea{{ls}}e, and you tribulation: but by an equalitie. {{verse|chapter=8|verse=14|align=float}}† Let in this pre{{ls}}ent time your {{sup|‖}} aboundance {{ls}}upplie their want: that their aboundance al{{ls}}o may {{ls}}upplie your vvant, that there be an equalitie, {{verse|chapter=8|verse=15|align=float}}† as it is vvritten: * {{outside R|''Exo. 16, 28.''}} ''He that had much, abounded not: and he that had litle, vvanted not''.⊣
